item.title: AI and Writing: Academic Integrity and Your Voice
item.description: Wednesday, October 14th, 2026: 3:00 PM - 4:00 PM Student Success Center, Folsom Library, 1st Floor In the age of AI, it is increasingly important to understand how AI can serve as an effective tool in the writing process, and what it means to use it with academic integrity. This workshop explores how to use AI effectively and responsibly while maintaining your own voice as a writer.

item.title: Alumni Weekend Side-by-Side Rehearsal with the RPI Symphony Orchestra
item.description: Experience the excitement of the RPI Symphony Orchestra as current students and alumni reunite for a special open rehearsal under the direction of Dr. Robert Whalen. This unique side-by-side event honors the alumni whose continued commitment and musicianship have helped shape the Orchestra’s tradition of excellence while offering a behind-the-scenes look at preparations for its 154th season. Join us on 10/10 at 1pm in DCC 308.
item.author: Community

item.title: Computer Science Colloquia - Sarah Dean - Recovering and Steering Belief States in Partially Observed Systems
item.description: Date: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 4:00 PM - 5:00 PM - Auto-regressive models, trained simply to predict future observations from past ones, have become a default tool for sequential data, from language to video to control-relevant time series. This talk first addresses that gap in a canonical setting and then concludes with a discussion of a class systems which captures these observer effects, recent results on learning and control, and several open questions.

item.description: Date: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 12:00 PM - 12:30 PM - Join RPI at Work Associate Dean Michael Hughes for a 30-minute information session covering RPI’s online, project-based Mechanical Engineering and Systems Engineering graduate degree programs. item.title: RPI Faculty In-Person Workshop - Getting to Know the Basics of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) within the Classroom
item.description: Date: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM - In this workshop we will look at some of the basics of AI, terminology, explore how prompts influence the responses these systems generate, and discuss tools available. As faculty and instructors, we don’t need to become AI experts. However, having a basic understanding of these tools can help us make thoughtful decisions about assignments and classroom expectations. Please click the link in the See section to register by Friday, October 9th…

item.title: Call for Survey Participants - First Generation Faculty & Staff
item.description:
As we prepare for our National First-Generation Student week November 3-7, the Office of Inclusive Excellence invites you to complete this short survey if you are a faculty or staff member who identifies—or has identified—as a first-generation college graduate- (defined as someone whose parent(s)/guardian(s) did not complete a four-year college degree).
